rows.acip: DE'I PHYIR SUN CI PHYIN DU RGOL BA GA LA YOD, GANG GIS NA RANG GI PHYOGS GZHAG TU MED CING GZHAN GYI PHYOGS BZLOG PA DON DAM PAR 'DOD PA'I MTSAN NYID BYAS PA 'DI, SUN CI PHYIN DU RGOL BA PA'I YANG DAG PA'I MTSAN NYID DU 'GYUR BA,
rows.wylie: de'i phyir sun ci phyin du rgol ba ga la yod, gang gis na rang gi phyogs gzhag tu med cing gzhan gyi phyogs bzlog pa don dam par 'dod pa'i mtshan nyid byas pa 'di, sun ci phyin du rgol ba pa'i yang dag pa'i mtshan nyid du 'gyur ba
rows.english: How then could there ever be an opponent that we overcame? Suppose that there were no position of our own that we could ever put forward, but that at the same time we posited some definitive statement that could put a stop to the other side's position. This would in itself require a definitive opponent—one that existed really, in order for us to overcome.

rows.acip: STONG PA NYID BDEN PAS STONG PAR GSUNGS PA NI STONG NYID DAM CHOS NYID LA DNGOS PO STE BDEN PAR 'DZIN PA'I BLO CAN GYI BDEN PAR 'DZIN PA BZLOG PAR BYA BA'I PHYIR RGYAL BA'I YUM LAS GSUNGS PA YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: stong pa nyid bden pas stong par gsungs pa ni stong nyid dam chos nyid la dngos po ste bden par 'dzin pa'i blo can gyi bden par 'dzin pa bzlog par bya ba'i phyir rgyal ba'i yum las gsungs pa yin no
rows.english: These statements that emptiness itself is empty of any true existence were made in the Mother Sutras themselves, in order to block the tendency to hold things as being real, in the thoughts of those whose minds were already grasping to the idea that things could be real: who were holding that emptiness or ultimate reality itself was a real thing.

rows.english: The fact that all ten directions of east and the rest are empty of existing through any essential nature of their own is “great emptiness.” And it was taught in order to stop people from holding that the directions are vast in a way that exists through some nature of its own. An example of taking the directions in a mistaken way would be where the River school called the Detailers holds that a direction represents some perfectly unchanging substance. 6) Ultimate emptiness

rows.acip: 'DI NI TING 'DZIN RGYAL PO LAS, YOD MED DANG GTZANG MI GTZANG GI MTHA' GNYIS SPANGS NAS, DBUS LA'ANG GNAS PAR MI BYED DO, ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR MTHA' SPANGS PA'I DBUS BDEN NAM SNYAM PA'I BDEN 'DZIN BZLOG PA'I PHYIR DU GSUNGS PA STE,
rows.wylie: 'di ni ting 'dzin rgyal po las, yod med dang gtsang mi gtsang gi mtha' gnyis spangs nas, dbus la'ang gnas par mi byed do, zhes gsungs pa ltar mtha' spangs pa'i dbus bden nam snyam pa'i bden 'dzin bzlog pa'i phyir du gsungs pa ste
rows.english: All this recalls for example the King of Concentration, where it says that we should give up pairs of extremes such as existing or not existing; or else being clean or not being clean; but that neither should we then stay somewhere in the middle between these extremes. This was spoken to help us stop our habit of wondering whether or not the view in the middle might exist in truth, once we have eliminated the two extremes in each case.

rows.acip: DE LTAR BSHAD PA LAS BZLOG PA NI GNAS MIN PA ZHES BYA STE, DPER NA DGE BA LAS RNAM SMIN YID DU MI 'ONG BA 'BYUNG BA DANG, MTHONG LAM THOB PAS LAS DBANG GIS SRID PA BRGYAD PA 'GRUB PA NI GNAS MA YIN ZHING GO SKABS MED PA LTA BU'O,,
rows.wylie: de ltar bshad pa las bzlog pa ni gnas min pa zhes bya ste, dper na dge ba las rnam smin yid du mi 'ong ba 'byung ba dang, mthong lam thob pas las dbang gis srid pa brgyad pa 'grub pa ni gnas ma yin zhing go skabs med pa lta bu'o
rows.english: Anything that could happen in the opposite way from what we have described here then would be called what is “not actual.” For example, it would not be actual (there would be no chance of it) if a virtuous action led to an unpleasant ripening; or if an individual had attained the path of seeing and then—due to the power of karma—were to experience an eighth rebirth afterwards.

rows.english: And then there are cases of the opposite of these two; meaning that the karmas are mixed. And then there are the great variety of different ripenings that are produced by this path.

rows.english: What is the Reason for this? It is all because Those who are Not well versed Still possess A state of mind Where they have Strong craving. And because of this, They undergo Periods when they Are born & destroyed. They are torn From what feels Attractive, and Meet with The undesirable; They achieve The future fate of Those who still have Terrible deeds. The world Has crowded to Worthy objects Of compassion. As such, you— The Conqueror— Have, out of This compassion, Turned your heart Away from peace, Without allowing Yourself to go Into nirvana.

rows.wylie: 'jig rten gyi skye bo de rnams thugs brtse ba chen po'i yul du rab tu dong ba ste song bas na, thugs rje chen pos bcom ldan 'das khyod kyi thugs zhi ba phyogs gcig pa la gzhol ba las bzlog pas khyod la zhi ba phyogs gcig pa'i mya ngan las 'das pa mi mnga' bar 'jig rten du bzhugs so
rows.english: The beings of this world have “crowded to”—have become—worthy objects of great compassion. As such, “you”—the Conqueror—have, out of this great compassion, turned away from allowing your heart to be lost to but a partial state of peace. That is, you remain here in the world, but without allowing yourself to go into a kind of nirvana which represents one side of the condition of peace. How the commentary was composed

rows.english: He held a high level of knowledge that was never stolen away; and he possessed compassion as well. He was known for sketching a cow that was about to give birth, and then milking real milk from it. With this, he was able to stop others from believing that things are real. This then is the one who completed this composition.

rows.english: We must then for the short term go for shelter to the Three Jewels, to keep ourselves from a birth in the lower realms. We must as well open up and admit the things we have done wrong before, and restrain ourselves in the future. To do so we must make strong and heartfelt use of the four forces that counteract the power of the wrong. We must too put all our effort into taking up even the smallest virtue, and giving up even the slightest harms we commit

rows.english: Every trace of vegetation— from the roots, to the stalks, to the branches, to the twigs, and out to the leaves, would be crushed to powder. And every livingcreature there, would be smashed to dust. And as the mountains fell in it would happen in a minute, and no one would be able to outrun them, or force them back, or buy them off. Nor but with the greatest difficulty could you use any kind of magic substance, or magic words, or any sort of elixir to stop them.

rows.english: And what are these four terrors? They are aging, and sickness, and death, and trouble. Great King, I say to you: aging is the fact that our vitality is inevitably obliterated; sickness is the fact that our health is inevitably obliterated; trouble is the fact that any good thing that ever comes to us is inevitably obliterated; and death is the fact that our very life is inevitably obliterated. All four of these come to us, and we cannot outrun them, Nor but with the greatest difficulty could you use any kind of magic substance, or magic words, or any sort of elixir to stop them.

rows.acip: DE YANG LTUNG BA PHYIR BCOS NI SDOM PA GONG 'OG SO SO NAS GSUNGS PA LTAR BYA LA SDIG PA, PHYIR BCOS PA NI STOBS BZHI'I SGO NAS BYA STE CHOS BZHI BSTAN PA'I MDO LAS BYAMS PA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' SEMS DPA' CHEN PO CHOS BZHI DANG LDAN NA SDIG PA BYAS SHING BSAGS PA YANG ZIL GYIS GNON PAR 'GYUR RO BZHI GANG ZHE NA 'DI LTA STE RNAM PAR SUN 'BYIN PA KUN TU SPYOD PA DANG GNYEN PO KUN TU SPYOD PA DANG NYES PA LAS BZLOG PA'I STOBS DANG RTEN GYI STOBS SO ZHES GSUNGS TE BYAS SHING BSAGS PA'I LAS NI MYONG NGES YIN PAS DE ZIL GYIS GNON NUS NA MA NGES PA LTA CI SMOS

rows.english: Instances in which you have committed some transgression of your vows, at whichever level of vows you may have, should be repaired according to the methods prescribed for those particular vows. For repairing the damage caused by other kinds of bad deeds you should utilize the four powers. As the Sutra on the Four Practices states, O Loving One, if a great bodhisattva keeps four practices, then he or she can never be overwhelmed by bad deeds that they have both committed and collected. And what are these four practices? They are the activity of destruction, and the activity of an antidote, and the power of restoring, and the power of the The expression "committed and collected" refers to actions whose karmic results are "certain to be experienced." If even these types of karmic results can be overcome by the four practices, then there is no need to mention those which are not certain to be experienced. An Original Source for the Principle that Old Karma Can be Removed The general principle that old karma can be removed from our mind streams is clearly stated in a number of important works by Lord Buddha himself. One of the most famous of these is a part from the famous Diamond-Cutter Sutra, which appears in the following selection in bold lettering. The commentary that follows the sutra is the only known native Tibetan explanation of the work, and was composed by Chone Drakpa Shedrup (1675-1748) of the incomparable Sera Mey Tibetan Monastery. Chone Lama skillfully weaves the root text into his explanation, and these words have also been printed in bold. He moreover quotes several other important original sources to demonstrate that old karma can be removed.

rows.english: A person who relies on the Wish in the form of a prayer can rip out, from its roots, the obstacle created by the deed they've committed. There are a number of references we could use to demonstrate this fact. The young man named "Child of the Friend" wanted to travel across the sea to another land; his mother, for sheer love of the boy, would kneel and grasp him by his two legs, and was thus able to stop him. There came a point though where he was seized by violent anger at her, and he hit her on the head with his leg. Then he went to sea, but his ship went down in a storm. There was a near-hell at the edge of the ocean, and here the karma seed from disrespecting his mother was awakened. He heard a voice from the sky that said "Kneel here, for the crown of knives is about to spin down upon your head." And he stood, making to himself a fervent prayer: May the karma of all those who have ever disrespected their mother in the past; or who are disrespecting their mother at this moment; or who may ever in the future disrespect their mother all ripen upon me alone, at this very moment. May no one else ever suffer the pain that I am about to undergo.

rows.english: It is stated in scripture as well that each and every one of the twelve links in the chain of interdependence depends on a single thing: the mind. These references convey yet another meaning of the word "only" in the expression "mind-only." Here the point is that mind is the main thing. The former scriptural references are putting their point in a negative way, and the latter references are putting their point in a positive way. Thus we can see that it's the mind which is the one single principal cause that sets all life into motion. The principal cause is not something other than the mind. Therefore when the sutras speak of "mind only," they are making the point that mind is the main thing, and not matter. Although we do of course admit that physical matter exists, this matter is not the one prime creator of sentient beings in the way that mind is. Therefore all these scriptural references are denying that the opposite of the mind, something other than the mind, could be the creator. They are not though saying that there are no outside physical objects at all. The Asian Classics Institute Reading Two: How Emptiness Allows Karma to Work, According to the Middle-Way School

rows.wylie: 'o na shAn+ti pas dgra nag 'grel par, smad mi bya zhes bya ba ni rtsod pas sun dbyung bar mi bya ste 'gro ba dag ni rang rang gi 'dun pa'i theg pa tsam las rim gyis 'jus shing byang chub par 'gyur gyi btsan thabs su 'dun pa bzlog pa ni sdang ba 'phel ba'i rgyu tsam yin pas bzhag ste, zhes grub mtha' 'dzin pa sun 'byin pa la smod par gsungs pa ji ltar yin snyam na, sngags sam mtshan nyid kyi theg pa la skyon bkal nas bka' ma yin no, ,zhes sun phyung ba na de dag gi grub mtha' 'dzin pa'i yang 'dun pa ldog pa la bshad pas skyon med do
rows.english: "Well then," you may ask.  "How does it fit in here when Shantipa, in his commentary to the Ebony Enemy, describes the act of disparaging here as overthrowing the belief of a particular school?  He says, When the wording of the vow here says that we should "never disparage their beliefs," what it means is that we should not seek to overthrow others" beliefs through argument.  The point is that beings reach enlightenment by being taken up gradually, without overextending themselves past the particular way which they find comfortable at any given time.  If instead we undertake some drastic step to try to change their minds, it only causes hard feelings--and so for the time being we should let it be." And yet there's no problem here.  What Shantipa is referring to here is where we say something negative about either the secret or open ways of Buddhism, overthrowing it in the sense of saying "This is not the Word of the Buddha," and thus changing the person's mind: causing them to give up their desire to learn a particular school of Buddhism.

rows.acip: BLA MA'I DRUNG DU GZHAN GYIS PHYAG BYA BA SOGS BZLOG PA,
rows.wylie: bla ma'i drung du gzhan gyis phyag bya ba sogs bzlog pa
rows.english: If in our Lama's presence another person attempts to prostrate to us or anything of that nature, then we must stop them from doing so. B. The Mother Vows, Part One Our final group of tantric vows is the Mother Vows.  In this and the final class, we present the entire text of an extremely rare and secret commentary on these vows by the famed Mongolian sage, Kalka Damtsik Dorje (1781-1855).  His work is entitled The Shining Glory of Great Bliss: A Presentation of the Eight Pledges Spoken in the Root Tantra of Highest Bliss (bDe-mchog rtza-rgyud las gsungs pa'i dam-tsig brgyad gyi rnam-bzhag bde-chen dpal-'gyur). As we will see, this text draws large sections verbatim from Je Tsongkapa's own Cow that Produces Every Wish: An Extensive Explanation of the Practice of Realization for the Secret Teaching of the Conqueror, the Glorious Sphere of Highest Bliss (Heruka), found at ACIP digital text S5320. ***

rows.english: You can also read the lines as saying that Crowface and the rest of the eight Guardians cause your respect and devotion to come to increase; and that these emotions are the cause of every spiritual attainment.  The point here is that, as we noted before, the cause of every spiritual attainment is to always (meaning continually) feel respect for one's Lama and for deep practitioners who follow this secret teaching.  And the Guardians of the Gates can help us stop any hindrances which might prevent this respect and faith from growing ever higher; as such, they are causes that help these emotions increase.

rows.acip: GRVA PA GZHAN GYI PHRAG DOG GIS DMAG DRANGS BYUNG BA SPRUL PA'I DMAG GIS PHYIR BZLOG PAS GUS SHING SLOB MAR GYUR, THANG LHA DANG SHAB KYI 'BA' RA NAG PO LA SOGS PA BAR CHAD BYED DU BYUNG BA'I LHA 'DRE RNAMS NYIN MO THOG DANG MTSAN MO TING NGE 'DZIN GYIS ZIL GYIS MNAN ZHING SROG SNGAGS BLANGS TE DAM TSIG LA BZHAG
rows.wylie: grva pa gzhan gyi phrag dog gis dmag drangs byung ba sprul pa'i dmag gis phyir bzlog pas gus shing slob mar gyur, thang lha dang shab kyi 'ba' ra nag po la sogs pa bar chad byed du byung ba'i lha 'dre rnams nyin mo thog dang mtshan mo ting nge 'dzin gyis zil gyis mnan zhing srog sngags blangs te dam tshig la bzhag
rows.english: At one point it happened that some other monks, out of envy towards Kyungpo Neljor, actually organized a group of armed men to do Him violence.  He routed the soldiers though by emanating an army of His own, which grained the monks' respect, and they became His disciples. In these days too a great many spirit beings of obstruction made their appearance—demons such as the Spirit of the Plains, and the Ebony Devil of Shab.  When they came in the daytime, Kyungpo Neljor blasted them with bolts of lightning; those who came at night He overwhelmed with the power of His meditation.  Then He used mantras to capture their life-force, and bound them to His service.

rows.acip: 'PHO BA NI, 'CHI LTAS BYUNG MA THAG NAS 'PHO BA BYED DU MI RUNG BAS 'CHI LTAS BYUNG NA 'CHI BA BLU BA'I THABS GANG ZAB LA 'BAD DGOS, 'CHI BLU BYAS KYANG MI BZLOG PA BYUNG NA, ZLA BA DRUG GI GONG ROL NAS 'PHO BA BYA CHOG ,

rows.english: Here are some notes on the practice of transferring your mind.  Transferring your mind this way is not something you should be doing right after you get a sign that you are going to die.  Therefore when such a sign occurs you should put all your effort into carrying out the deepest practice you can find for ransoming death.  If you do complete one of these practices and are still unable to reverse your impending death, then six months before it comes you are allowed to do the transfer.

rows.english: And then the Master decided to return to the city, for three reasons.  First of all, He wanted to put a stop to the lack of faith that people were feeling towards Him, by showing them the pureness of His actions.  He further wanted to accomplish the purpose for which the emanation of the Compassionate One had been invited, in order to help lower kinds of living beings in the future.  And then thirdly He had the idea that He could get the people of the country of Oddivisha to enter the diamond way.  He set off then for the city, bringing along with him a little boy and a little girl that He had emanated.

rows.english: When they state this way that--if you can't find an outer woman, then you can practice with an imaginary one--it's with reference to the fact that practice with an imaginary partner doesn't have the capacity to bring on in us the meditation of great bliss in the same way that practice with an actual partner does.  To say though that you do find an outer woman, and then leave off practicing with Her, and practice instead with an imaginary woman, is to interpret the lines in a completely opposite way than what we've seen above.

rows.acip: YAN LAG BCU GNYIS PO THAMS CAD KYANG SEMS GCIG LA BRTEN PAR GSUNGS PA LA BRTEN NAS, TZAM GYI SGRAS SEMS GTZO BOR GYUR PAR BSTAN TE, BSHAD PA SNGA MA DGAG PHYOGS DANG PHYI MA SGRUB PHYOGS NAS YIN NO, , DE'I PHYIR 'GRO BA RAB TU 'JUG PA LA SEMS NYID GTZO BO'I RGYU YIN GYI, SEMS LAS GZHAN PA NI GTZO BO'I RGYU MIN PAS, MDO LAS SEMS TZAM ZHIG GTZO BOR BZHAG GI GZUGS NI MA YIN NO, , GAL TE GZUGS YOD PAR 'DOD MOD KYI STE KYANG GZUGS DE LA NI SEMS BZHIN DU 'GRO BA'I BYED PA PO NYID NI YOD PA MA YIN NO, , DES NA SEMS LAS GZHAN PA'I BYED PA PO BZLOG PA STE BKAG GI, PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS NI BKAG PA MA YIN NO, ,
rows.wylie: yan lag bcu gnyis po thams cad kyang sems gcig la brten par gsungs pa la brten nas, tsam gyi sgras sems gtso bor gyur par bstan te, bshad pa snga ma dgag phyogs dang phyi ma sgrub phyogs nas yin no, , de'i phyir 'gro ba rab tu 'jug pa la sems nyid gtso bo'i rgyu yin gyi, sems las gzhan pa ni gtso bo'i rgyu min pas, mdo las sems tsam zhig gtso bor bzhag gi gzugs ni ma yin no, , gal te gzugs yod par 'dod mod kyi ste kyang gzugs de la ni sems bzhin du 'gro ba'i byed pa po nyid ni yod pa ma yin no, , des na sems las gzhan pa'i byed pa po bzlog pa ste bkag gi, phyi rol gyi gzugs ni bkag pa ma yin no,
rows.english: It is stated in scripture as well that each and every one of the twelve links in the chain of interdependence depends on a single thing: the mind. These references convey yet another meaning of the word "only" in the expression "mind-only." Here the point is that mind is the main thing. The former scriptural references are putting their point in a negative way, and the latter references are putting their point in a positive way. Thus we can see that it's the mind which is the one single principal cause that sets all life into motion. The principal cause is not something other than the mind. Therefore when the sutras speak of "mind only," they are making the point that mind is the main thing, and not matter. Although we do of course admit that physical matter exists, this matter is not the one prime creator of sentient beings in the way that mind is. Therefore all these scriptural references are denying that the opposite of the mind, something other than the mind, could be the creator. rows.english: It is stated in scripture as well that each and every one of the twelve links in the chain of interdependence depends on a single thing: the mind. These references convey yet another meaning of the word "only" in the expression "mind-only." Here the point is that mind is the main thing. The former scriptural references are putting their point in a negative way, and the latter references are putting their point in a positive way. Thus we can see that it's the mind which is the one single principal cause that sets all life into motion. The principal cause is not something other than the mind. Therefore when the sutras speak of "mind only," they are making the point that mind is the main thing, and not matter. Although we do of course admit that physical matter exists, this matter is not the one prime creator of sentient beings in the way that mind is. Therefore all these scriptural references are denying that the opposite of the mind, something other than the mind, could be the creator. They are not though saying that there are no outside physical objects at all. 93 The Asian Classics Institute Course V: How Karma Works Reading Six: How Emptiness Allows Karma to Work, According to the Middle-Way School

rows.english: The question and answer that appear in the first two sentences serve to identify constructs as what are being referred to when we speak of "things that lack any definitive nature." The part that begins with "And why do we speak of them as such?" serves as an answer to the question of what reason there is for us to describe them as such. Then Lord Buddha answers by giving us two reasons: one from the negative point of view, where he says that these things do not exist by definition; and one from the positive point of view, where he says that they are established through names and terms. The way in which the sutra approaches the question from these two different aspects can be understood to apply to the latter two attributes as well.
